title.en: An extended metaphor in a personal essay
title.es: Metáfora extendida en un ensayo personal

es: Sostener una metáfora extendida en un ensayo personal sin mezclar imágenes: abrir con la metáfora, desarrollarla con elementos del mismo campo y cerrar con una reflexión que diga en sentido literal lo aprendido.

teaching.en: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is one more step along a road that I can only see a few metres ahead.
teaching.es: Aprender inglés es un largo viaje, y cada clase es un paso más por un camino del que solo veo unos pocos metros por delante.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora extendida: abres con la imagen (journey) y la sigues con elementos del mismo campo, como step.
segments: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is one more step
along a road that I can only see a few metres ahead.
teaching.audioText: Learning English is a long journey, and every lesson is one more step along a road that I can only see a few metres ahead.

teaching.en: Grammar is my map and vocabulary is my compass, so even when the road is unclear I can still find my direction.
teaching.es: La gramática es mi mapa y el vocabulario es mi brújula, así que aun cuando el camino no está claro puedo encontrar mi dirección.
teaching.explanationEs: Cada parte del aprendizaje recibe un elemento del viaje (map, compass): así la imagen se sostiene.
segments: Grammar is my map and vocabulary is my compass, so even
when the road is unclear I can still find my direction.
teaching.audioText: Grammar is my map and vocabulary is my compass, so even when the road is unclear I can still find my direction.

teaching.en: Sometimes I feel lost, but each mistake shows me where the road turns, and that helps me stay on course.
teaching.es: A veces me siento perdido, pero cada error me muestra dónde gira el camino, y eso me ayuda a mantener el rumbo.
teaching.explanationEs: Sigues en el mismo campo: perdido, camino, giro, rumbo. Stay on course = no desviarte de tu objetivo.
segments: Sometimes I feel lost, but each mistake shows me where
the road turns, and that helps me stay on course.
teaching.audioText: Sometimes I feel lost, but each mistake shows me where the road turns, and that helps me stay on course.

teaching.en: To sustain a metaphor, choose one field and keep every new detail inside it, so that the essay remains coherent from the first line to the last.
teaching.es: Para sostener una metáfora, elige un campo y mantén cada detalle nuevo dentro de él, de modo que el ensayo sea coherente de la primera línea a la última.
teaching.explanationEs: Sustain = mantener algo a lo largo del tiempo; coherent = con todas las partes bien unidas.
segments: To sustain a metaphor, choose one field and keep every new detail inside it,
so that the essay remains coherent from the first line to the last.
teaching.audioText: To sustain a metaphor, choose one field and keep every new detail inside it, so that the essay remains coherent from the first line to the last.

teaching.en: If vocabulary is my compass but grammar is my sword, the image becomes mixed, and the reader wonders whether I am travelling or fighting.
teaching.es: Si el vocabulario es mi brújula pero la gramática es mi espada, la imagen queda mezclada y el lector se pregunta si viajo o si peleo.
teaching.explanationEs: Una espada no pertenece a un viaje: mezclar campos confunde al lector.
segments: If vocabulary is my compass but grammar is my sword, the image
becomes mixed, and the reader wonders whether I am travelling or fighting.
teaching.audioText: If vocabulary is my compass but grammar is my sword, the image becomes mixed, and the reader wonders whether I am travelling or fighting.

teaching.en: Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed, and that the destination is only the end of one road.
teaching.es: Mirando atrás, el viaje me enseñó que la paciencia importa más que la velocidad, y que el destino es solo el final de un camino.
teaching.explanationEs: Cierre reflexivo: Looking back + lección dicha ya en sentido literal (patience matters more than speed).
segments: Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed,
and that the destination is only the end of one road.
teaching.audioText: Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed, and that the destination is only the end of one road.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase rompe la metáfora de la montaña en este párrafo?

choices.text: Grammar is my rope, vocabulary is my boots.
Sometimes I feel that I am sailing without a map.
The top is speaking well, and I must climb slowly and carefully.

feedback.es: Navegar pertenece al mar, no a la montaña: rompe la imagen, mientras que la cuerda, las botas y la cima son elementos de una escalada.

hint.es: Busca el elemento que no pertenece a una escalada.

origin.text: Learning English is a mountain. Grammar is my rope, vocabulary is my boots, and the top is speaking well. But sometimes I feel that I am sailing without a map, and then I must climb more slowly.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es difícil mantener una metáfora a lo largo de todo un ensayo.»

feedback.es: Sustain a metaphor significa mantenerla viva de principio a fin sin cambiar de imagen.

hint.es: Es el verbo de «sostener» que aparece en la enseñanza de esta clase.

origin.text: It is difficult to ___ a metaphor over a whole essay, because every new detail has to stay inside the same image.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada error es un giro del camino que me enseña paciencia.»

answer.text: Every mistake is a turn in the road that teaches me patience

feedback.es: El error se presenta como un giro del camino y that teaches me patience cierra la frase con la lección.

hint.es: Empieza con Every mistake y termina con la palabra patience.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué advertencia hace la hablante sobre el «jardín».

choices.text: That words planted in the wrong season will not grow.
That watering the words every day is a waste of effort.
That progress cannot be rushed, however hard you try.

feedback.es: La advertencia es que nadie puede tirar de una flor para que crezca antes: el progreso necesita paciencia y no se acelera.

origin.audio: Learning a language is a garden, she said. At first you plant a few words, then you water them every day, and months later some of them become flowers. But she warned that a garden also needs patience, because nobody can pull a flower to make it grow faster.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada elemento del viaje con la idea del aprendizaje.

pairs.es: un error que obliga a cambiar de dirección
las reglas de gramática que te guían

feedback.es: En una metáfora extendida cada elemento del viaje representa una parte del aprendizaje: error, vocabulario, meta y reglas.

pairs.es: un error que obliga a cambiar de dirección
las reglas de gramática que te guían

prompt.es: Completa: «Mirando atrás, veo cuánto he avanzado.»

feedback.es: Looking back abre el cierre reflexivo y mira el camino recorrido para extraer una lección.

origin.text: Looking ___, I can see how far I have come, although at the time every single step felt small and slow.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le recomienda la profesora a la alumna en su comentario?

choices.text: To keep the journey image all the way to the ending.
To replace the journey with a fighting image throughout.
To add a second image in the closing line for contrast.

feedback.es: La profesora aprecia el viaje y critica el cambio a la batalla: recomienda conservar una sola imagen hasta el cierre.

origin.text: Teacher's comment: 'Your first three paragraphs build a clear journey. In the last one, however, vocabulary suddenly becomes a sword and every mistake becomes a fight. The reader stops travelling and starts fighting. Keep one image, and your closing line will feel earned.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué deja entender el hablante sobre sus primeros meses.

choices.text: He progressed slowly, but he enjoyed every lesson.
He felt disappointed and came close to giving up.
He compared himself with others and decided to study less.

feedback.es: «For months nothing seemed to happen, and I almost gave up» muestra desánimo y casi abandono; el progreso llegó después.

origin.audio: To be honest, learning Spanish was like growing a garden. I planted a few words, watered them with practice and waited. For months nothing seemed to happen, and I almost gave up, because every week I compared myself with people who seemed to learn faster. Then, one morning, I understood a whole conversation on the bus, and I felt so happy that I wanted to tell everybody. Looking back, patience was the best water, although I did not know it then.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un día llegaré a mi destino, pero el camino ya me ha enseñado más.»

feedback.es: Reach + destination es la colocación natural para llegar a la meta; arrive necesitaría la preposición at.

origin.text: One day I will ___ my destination, but I already know that the road itself has taught me more than the arrival will.

prompt.es: Escribe un ensayo con una metáfora extendida sobre aprender un idioma.

answer.text: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning I was standing at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a wrong turn that showed me a new direction. Sometimes the road was long and I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns any more. I still stay on course because I practise every day, even when I am tired, and my friends walk beside me and help me laugh at every wrong turn. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.
accepted: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning I was standing at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a wrong turn that showed me a new direction. Sometimes the road was long and I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns any more. I still stay on course because I practise every day, even when I am tired, and my friends walk beside me and help me laugh at every wrong turn. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.

Learning English is a garden. On the first day I planted a few words, and every morning I watered them with a little practice. Some words grew quickly and others needed more time, but I never stopped planting. Grammar was the ground, and my mistakes were the bad plants that I took out one by one. My teacher was a patient gardener, and my friends were the sun. Sometimes it was hard, and I felt lost in the garden, but I stayed on course by returning every day. Looking back, the garden taught me that patience matters more than speed. Today I have a few flowers, and I am happy, but I will keep planting new words every day. In the end, the flowers did not come quickly, but they came, and I am proud of every single one of them.

feedback.es: Un buen ensayo abre con la metáfora, la desarrolla con elementos del mismo campo, incluye una dificultad y cierra con una reflexión literal.

origin.text: Escribe un ensayo de unas 140 palabras (mínimo 126) sobre aprender un idioma. Abre con una sola metáfora extendida (por ejemplo, un viaje), desarróllala con al menos tres elementos de esa imagen, incluye una dificultad y cierra con una reflexión (por ejemplo, con «Looking back»).

prompt.es: ¿Qué elemento rompe la imagen del jardín en este ensayo?

choices.text: Every mistake is a weed that I pull out.
I plant words and water them with practice.
My teacher is a train that never stops.

feedback.es: El tren no pertenece a un jardín; plantar, regar y arrancar malas hierbas sí mantienen la imagen.

origin.text: Essay: 'Learning English is a garden. I plant words, I water them with practice, and every mistake is a weed that I pull out. Lately, though, my teacher is a train that never stops, and I cannot keep up with it.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Una lección breve cada día me ayuda a mantener el rumbo.»

feedback.es: Stay on course significa no desviarte de tu objetivo durante el viaje; en una metáfora de viaje es el rumbo que mantienes (también se acepta stay on track).

origin.text: A short lesson every day helps me stay on ___, even when the road is long and I am tired.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué función cumple este cierre dentro del ensayo.

choices.text: It states in plain words what the writer learned.
It opens a second metaphor about a new experience.
It lists the steps needed to reach the destination.

feedback.es: El cierre resume la lección (confiar en el camino, seguir andando despacio) sin abrir otra imagen ni dar instrucciones.

origin.audio: Looking back, I see that the road was long, and that most of the time I did not know where I was going. But every wrong turn taught me something, and I now trust the road more than the map. I will keep walking, slowly, because that is what the journey has taught me.
